articleTitle: Image processing transputer-based machine for mobile robot road-following
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transputers for Image Processing Applications
abstract: Reports recent work on the mobile robot project underway at the University of Bristol. The aim of the project is to explore mobile robot road-following algorithms and suitable hardware architectures to run these algorithms. The prototype hardware, designed and built at the University, is a real-time frame grabber system based on transputers. The system is capable of concurrently grabbing, processing and displaying 256*256 8-bit pixel images from a camera or video recorder. The authors describe algorithms which have been implemented on the transputer network to achieve near real-time execution on sequences of video data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel processing on transputer arrays for the recognition of objects in infra-red images
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transputers for Image Processing Applications
abstract: Previous work has shown that a simple measure of the shape of the autocorrelation function is a useful discriminant for target classification in infra-red images. It has been found that it is possible to recognise vehicles from texture information and, because object shape information is not used, it is well suited to thermal imagers which may not resolve shape or edge details. The algorithms in the paper have been adapted and developed for evaluation on arrays of transputers. Much experience has been gained in the design and development of algorithms and the approach required for efficient use of transputers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multi-transputer processor for high level image processing algorithms
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transputers for Image Processing Applications
abstract: A multi-transputer processor designed for the tasks of performing high level image processing algorithms and overall system management is discussed. The partitioning of a complete image processing system containing such a processor and its required interfaces is described. Hardware and software performance requirements are explained and details of achieved performance given. It is concluded that a processor such as that to be described is suitable for use in very high speed image processing systems and that under some circumstances, it is also possible to perform ancillary tasks within the processor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A pyramidal architecture for knowledge-based sonar image interpretation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transputers for Image Processing Applications
abstract: Describes a pyramidal architecture for Knowledge-Based sonar image interpretation. The architecture will finally use the Inmos T800 Transputer as its basic processing agent. A Knowledge-Based System (KBS), is one approach which attempts to encode the knowledge and expertise required to reason in a specific problem domain. This knowledge is coded as a series of rules and facts and forms the Knowledge-Base of the system. However, KBS systems are often computationally intensive and to date, real-time response characteristics have not been apparent. By utilising a pyramidal architecture which pulls on techniques developed in the parallel processing community, a system is being designed and implemented which will provide this real-time performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel tomographic image reconstruction on transputer arrays
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transputers for Image Processing Applications
abstract: Tomographic Image Reconstruction forms an important element of non-invasive medical diagnosis. Here, 2D cross-sectional information of a 3D object is reconstructed from equiangular X-Ray projection data. Several algorithms have been proposed to solve the inverse problem of Image Reconstruction, however, the Fourier Backprojection (FBP) Algorithm is the most widely used method due to its speed and robustness, being a direct, non-iterative solution. Current technology is geared to the fastest possible implementation of FBP which includes the use of specialised hardware and array processors. It is the high cost and narrow specification of these machines that has promoted this investigation of the suitability of a transputer array implementation. In this paper, a parallel implementation of the FBP algorithm is proposed and an assessment of its viability is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transputer based super resolution of SAR images: two approaches to a parallel solution
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transputers for Image Processing Applications
abstract: Considers the parallel implementation on a transputer array of an algorithm for the super-resolution of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images. The authors consider two different approaches, both of which involve serial code running on a single master transputer, communicating with parallel code running on an array of slave transputers, where parallel code is only developed for those parts of the algorithm where the computation time justifies this. Firstly they take the simplest form of the super-resolution algorithm and parallelize the very large computations involved. Secondly they port the existing fast serial code to a single transputer, and develop parallel versions of selected routines where needed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An interactive image processing system based on a transputer tree network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transputers for Image Processing Applications
abstract: Describes the parallel implementation of an interactive image processing system based on a ternary tree configuration of transputers. The tree can be extended to utilise available processors. Approximately 100 image processing algorithms have been implemented, involving low level transformations, feature extraction, and preliminary scene interpretation. Dynamic load balancing techniques have been utilised extensively in order to distribute the workload and data around the processors for these operations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Image processing and video rate I/O on transputer arrays
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transputers for Image Processing Applications
abstract: A modular transputer array with fast I/O has been designed and built for distributed real time TV image processing. It is intended that a version of the transputer array will be used to support the SP4 division, RSRE, object recognition autonomous vehicle research programmes. The design philosophy is that all the data is made available to all the transputers in the array irrespective of need, thereby making for flexibility and ease of algorithm design. A novel scheme for recombining the data from the transputer array elements in real time either for display or further processing is also provided. In addition this work has led to the design of a low cost, low power, reduced component stand alone image processor which is described briefly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transputer implementation of the Radon transform
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transputers for Image Processing Applications
abstract: Describes a multi-transputer network which is capable of performing Radon transforms within a few seconds. Results show that linear features in noisy images can be rapidly enhanced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coordination in transputer and biological image processing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transputers for Image Processing Applications
abstract: Discusses a project to develop a computer vision system for active perceptual tasks such as camera focussing and positioning, and object recognition. The approach has been to utilise principles which have been shown to work in animal visual systems, and implement them using a transputer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
